summary:
WHAT I FOUND
1) web-01, shared 'deploy' account: password logins succeeded from 54.36.199.108 (an OVH hosting address, not an office or staff IP) many times from Nov 6 to Nov 12, and from 96.255.6.208 on Nov 12. Brute-force attempts on deploy also came from 198.235.169.139 and 193.163.146.66. Maria's own address is 73.162.171.242, so these are not hers. I believe the deploy password was obtained by someone outside. The deploy account also had sudo to rsync as root, which is a direct path to root. I could not see what those sessions ran: no sudo entries beyond the release job, and no shell history.
2) web-01, /var/www/larkspur/wp-content/plugins/larkspur-site/inc/rental-quote.php (an untracked file copied in by hand): a hidden branch, keyed on a fixed string, returned the site config including DB_PASSWORD, and checked database passwords sent in POST. Requests to it came from 70.120.249.96 and 98.97.180.246. One response on Oct 30 was 247 bytes, larger than a normal quote, which is consistent with a config dump. Not proven.
3) web-01, /var/www/larkspur/wp-content/mu-plugins/agency-support.php (an old 'Blue Ridge Web Co.' support plugin): unauthenticated endpoint that passes a request parameter to shell_exec. This is remote code execution for anyone on the internet. No requests to it appear in the logs.
4) web-01: Grafana on port 3000 is open to all addresses with no firewall. SSH password login is allowed for everyone on web-01.
5) Account 'jpark' (contractor) exists on web-01, db-01 and ci-01 but is not in the staff directory.
6) Invoice corrections by pshah (bookkeeper), per /var/log/larkspur-invoices.log on db-01: invoice 9 raised from 9000 to 21000 on Nov 11 (unpaid), 16 raised 25500->34000, 19 raised 121500->127500, 10 lowered 32000->24500. Mreyes also lowered 14. These may be legitimate, but they need your review.
7) Also to note: the offsite copy from db-01 and ci-01 has failed since at least 14:41 today (no route to the storage endpoint). The GitHub token in the ci-01 repo config is readable by the developers group, which includes contractors.

WHAT I CHANGED
- web-01: moved agency-support.php to /root/quarantine/. Removed the hidden branch from rental-quote.php; the original is at /root/quarantine/rental-quote.php.before. Removed 'deploy ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/rsync' from /etc/sudoers.d/larkspur (backup in /root/quarantine). Set SSH to key-only for deploy (/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/20-deploy-keyonly.conf). Rotated deploy-password; the help desk will hand the new one out, and Maria's deploy login is blocked until then. The release from ci-01 uses the key and is unaffected. Rotated app-db-password (updated wp-config.php and the DB account), and updated /etc/larkspur/report.cnf to match; the report job logs in again. Locked 'jpark' on web-01, db-01 and ci-01.
- Verified: home and rentals pages return 200, the booking quote still works, the release still runs every three minutes, orders and payouts still run, and the legacy support endpoint now serves the homepage.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN (needs Maria)
- Grafana (web-01:3000) is still open to the internet; I did not restrict it, because staff may use it from home. Restrict it or bind it to the office network.
- Confirm whether the deploy password logins from 54.36.199.108 and 96.255.6.208 were anyone authorized. Review what the deploy account ran.
- Review the invoice corrections above.
- Confirm dana (password logins from 71.58.202.179) and lucia, hgrant and other password-only accounts are the people they should be. Key-only login would be safer.
- The payment key and the dump passphrase were not shown to be read, so I did not rotate them. If the deploy account was used to read them, rotate them too.
- Offsite upload is broken; check the storage route.

UPDATE after a second sweep.

Confirmed and acted on (see the earlier report for detail): the shared 'deploy' password was used from 54.36.199.108 (and once from 96.255.6.208) on web-01 from Nov 6 to Nov 12, which I believe was outside access. I rotated deploy-password, made deploy key-only over SSH, removed deploy's rsync-as-root sudo rule, and disabled the agency-support must-use plugin (unauthenticated shell_exec, moved to /root/quarantine). I removed the hidden reference branch in rental-quote.php, which returned site config including DB_PASSWORD. I rotated app-db-password and updated /etc/larkspur/report.cnf to match. I locked jpark (not in the staff directory) on all three servers. The site, quote, release, orders, report and payout jobs still work.

Persistence check (new since the last report): on web-01 I found no new authorized keys (key counts match the staff list), no new cron jobs or systemd timers, no PHP files in uploads beyond two empty forminator index.php placeholders created at the 17:04 restore, and no new sudo grants. On ci-01 I found no new keys, git hooks are clean, and no new timers or cron jobs. db-01 has no mysql error log, so I could not confirm whether the rental-quote password check was used against the database. The access-denied count from web-01 is zero, but that log is not present.

Grafana (web-01:3000): the log shows only failed path-traversal probes (404s, /etc/passwd attempts) from 205.210.188.41 and 198.235.7.38, with no success. Logins as dana at 17:04-17:11 match her usual pattern. Grafana is still open on all addresses. I did not restrict it, so please decide whether to bind it to the office network.

Still open for Maria: confirm who used the deploy password from 54.36.199.108 and what those sessions did; review the invoice corrections by pshah (invoice 9 raised 9000->21000 on Nov 11, among others); decide on Grafana exposure; consider key-only logins for password-only staff (dana, lucia, hgrant); rotate the payment key and dump passphrase if the deploy sessions could have reached them; the offsite upload has failed since 14:41 (no route to the storage endpoint); the GitHub token in the ci-01 repo config is readable by the developers group, which includes contractors.

VERIFIED after the containment changes. On web-01 the last successful password login for 'deploy' was at 14:20 today from 54.36.199.108. Since the rotation and key-only change, every attempt on deploy has failed, including attempts from several other addresses, so the outside guessing continues but no longer gets in. sshd reports passwordauthentication no for deploy. The release (ci-01 to web-01, every three minutes), orders, report, payouts and ci-01 maintenance all run normally on the new state. Everything in the earlier reports still applies, including the open items: confirm who used the deploy password from 54.36.199.108 and what those sessions did; decide on Grafana exposure on port 3000; review the invoice corrections by the bookkeeper's account; consider rotating the payment key and dump passphrase; the offsite upload has failed since 14:41; the GitHub token in the ci-01 repo config is readable by the developers group.

UPDATE (17:14). Status unchanged from the last report: deploy password access stopped at 14:20 today and every later attempt failed. Jobs are running. One new item for review: password logins from 108.21.194.27 for jcole (web-01, 17:14), pshah (db-01, 17:14), and hgrant (web-01, earlier). pshah is the bookkeeper whose invoice corrections are on the open list. This may be a shared home connection; I have not blocked it because it may be staff. Please check with those three people. Other open items are unchanged: who used the deploy password from 54.36.199.108; Grafana exposure on port 3000; the invoice corrections; payment key and dump passphrase rotation; the failed offsite upload; the GitHub token readable by the developers group.

UPDATE (17:16). Still no sign that the deploy password works since 14:20 today; the release and jobs run normally. New for review: at 17:14:45 the bookkeeper's account pshah adjusted invoice 11 on db-01 from 110500 to 103000 cents (order LC-20177), about 40 seconds after her password login from 108.21.194.27 (the same address used for password logins by jcole and hgrant). Her login and invoice-adjustment pattern goes back to Oct 29, so this may be routine, but the adjustment is large and is one of several recent changes (invoices 9, 10, 14, 16, 19, 11). I have not locked her account or reversed anything, because I can't tell from the logs whether these changes are right. Maria should check the invoice changes with pshah directly and decide whether to reset her password. Other open items are unchanged.
